notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics SaaS building an assistant + semantic search across customer docs. Began with Hosted API POC (embeddings + chat). After 8 weeks POC they saw good quality but costs spiky and traffic growth => exploring Dedicated for predictable unit economics and data isolation. Key ask: committed baseline for cost predictability, clear burst policy, overage rate, and ramp schedule for first 6 months.

POC highlights: - Hosted API POC completed 2026-01-28. Used embeddings for doc-search (20M docs internal), chat assistant for support triage. - Quality: recall/precision met target for top-k=5; latency OK for dev tests but 95p latency spikes under load. - Cost: hosted run estimated to be ~2.5x projected budget at scale due to high embed generation and peak chat bursts.

Stakeholders: - Alex Kim (CTO) primary decision maker - Serena Patel (Head of Product) product lead - Jordan Myers (InfoSec) security + compliance - Maya Chen (AE) Redwood lead - Owen Clarke (SE) technical lead - Priya Singh (CSM) post-sale/PT involvement.

Technical requirements / targets: - Workloads: high-throughput embeddings (batch indexing) + low-latency chat (support assistant). - Embeddings throughput target: steady-state 150 qps, burst to 600 qps for reindex windows. - Chat target: 30 concurrent active sessions, 95th perc latency < 300ms. - Model preference: open models with 8k-16k context, testing quantized 8-bit variants for cost. - Routing: primary Dedicated for production, fallback to Hosted API for overflow only. - Data: logs retained 90 days, KMS for key management, EU residency for subset of customer corp data.

Pricing/packaging negotiation notes: - Initial proposal (2026-02-24): 12-month commit @ $18k/month reserved capacity (equiv. 3x A100 e-sets), burst allowance 2x baseline for free, 150% overage rate thereafter. - Customer feedback: wants either lower initial commit (2x baseline) with a 90-day ramp and guaranteed upgrade schedule, or keep 3x baseline but add additional burst buffer + lower overage pct. - They requested a 30-day pilot on Dedicated (reduced pilot price) to validate latency and ops. - Discussed ramp schedule: month1 40% commit, month2 70%, month3 full commit. They want explicit SLAs for latency during ramp and rollback path to Hosted. - SE flagged model/kernel tuning time ~2-3 weeks to reach 95p latency target; include engineering effort estimate in commercial proposal.

Legal / Security: - InfoSec sent standard questionnaire 2026-02-27 (drive link above). - Data residency: require EU residency option for client data for EU customers. - Need SSO/SAML integration with SCIM provisioning; timeline: 3 weeks after contract.

Commercial ask from customer: - Clear overage pricing and predictable monthly spend for budgeting - Option to add burst credits that reset monthly - Ramp schedule tied to usage thresholds to avoid immediate overage charges - Prefer 12-month term but open to 9-month with higher per-month commitment if able to add programmatic ramp credits.

Quotes / Commit scenarios discussed: - Option A: 12m commit, baseline 3 units, burst 2x free, overage 120% of unit price => ARR est ~$216k - Option B: 12m commit, baseline 2 units + guaranteed 90-day ramp, add purchasable monthly burst pool (prepaid credits) => ARR est ~$156k - Option C: 9m higher-rate short-term commit to pilot then convert to 12m based on benchmarks.

Next tactical steps: - AE to deliver pricing v2 with two commit/ramp options by 2026-03-18 (Maya) - SE (Owen) to run Dedicated pilot plan + show 95p latency proof of concept on customer prompts (2-week bench) - Legal to review data residency clause and produce draft intro language (Redwood legal) - Finance to provide invoice/PO flow for prepaid burst credits.

Notes from last call (2026-03-03): "If we can get predictable spend and a soft ramp that protects us from overage in first 90 days, we'll sign a 12-month commit." — Alex Kim.

CRM shorthand: demo ok; POC success -> wants predictable cost + compliance; primary blocker = budget cadence + legal SLA on residency.
